subject: Clarify SOC 2 report end-moment definition & timezone for log evidence
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@fintechco.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: luke.han@bluebayaudit.com
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on report coverage end moment for SOC 2 Type II

Hi Ava,

We're working through our SOC 2 intake for FinTechCo and have one technical question about the report period you provided (2026-01-01 through 2026-06-30). Our security team needs to be precise when we pull logs for evidence. Specifically:

- When a report says it covers through 2026-06-30, do you interpret that as inclusive up to 23:59:59 on June 30 in a stated timezone, or is the end moment exclusive of that final second?
- Which timezone is used to interpret the end-of-day in the report language (UTC, company local, or auditor specified)?
- For log-based controls, will a point-in-time snapshot exported at 12:00 local time be acceptable evidence, or do you require continuous exports showing the entire last day up to the final second?

We attached a short questionnaire (SOC2_request_questionnaire.pdf) with the evidence items we think we'll need. Can you confirm how you and your auditor typically define the report cutoff so we can align our exports and time conversions?

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Security Operations
FinTechCo

Attachments: SOC2_request_questionnaire.pdf

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@fintechco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 2 Oct 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on report coverage end moment for SOC 2 Type II

Hi Samira,

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answer: our standard reporting language is intended to be inclusive, but there are a few important nuances I want to confirm with our audit lead and security engineering team before I give an authoritative statement. I am looping in Neha (SOC 2 lead) and Priyom (security eng) to weigh in.

Preliminarily: we typically express coverage in UTC in our public reports, and phrasing like through 2026-06-30 is meant to include events with timestamps on or before 2026-06-30 23:59:59 UTC. However, that is a de facto practice rather than a binding definition, so we'll ask BlueBay to confirm the auditor position and provide sample wording.

A few logistical notes so we can prepare the exact evidence you need:
- If you can provide exported log files with the earliest and latest event timestamps and an explicit timezone indicator, that will satisfy most requests. A CSV with header fields event_time and timezone is ideal.
- If your systems store local timestamps, include a mapping table for conversions to UTC.
- If you prefer to supply a point-in-time snapshot, include the retention policy and a note about whether rolling or immutable archives were used at the snapshot moment.

Luke, could you confirm the auditor interpretation and, if possible, attach a short bridge-letter template or example wording for customers who need a formal statement about inclusivity and timezone?

Next steps for us: Priyom and I will draft the requested log extract format and upload a sample to the shared drive link. Samira, once BlueBay confirms, we'll upload a bridge letter draft if required.

Best,
Ava Chen
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Luke Han <luke.han@bluebayaudit.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@fintechco.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2026 11:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarification on report coverage end moment for SOC 2 Type II

Hi Ava and Samira,

Thanks for including me. From the auditor perspective, the clearest approach is to define the coverage window with both endpoints inclusive and specify the timezone. We often recommend the following explicit wording for bridge letters or customer guidance:

  For the avoidance of doubt, the covered reporting period for the SOC 2 Type II report is inclusive of the start and end dates. Events with timestamps greater than or equal to 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z and less than or equal to 2026-06-30T23:59:59Z are considered within the audit period.

A couple of implementation notes:
- UTC is preferred for evidence submission because it avoids ambiguity; if logs are in a different timezone, provide the conversion mapping.
- For log-based controls you can provide either: (a) continuous exports covering the entire window, or (b) a point-in-time snapshot accompanied by the system retention policy and an immutable archive proof or export that demonstrates the snapshot is representative.
- If your telemetry is sampled or aggregated, include the sampling policy and any translation logic.

I've attached two useful artifacts: a bridge letter template you can edit (bridge_letter_template.docx) and a small CSV example showing the event_time header and UTC-converted timestamps (log_extract_sample.csv). If you want, I can edit a draft bridge letter for FinTechCo once you upload it to the shared Drive.

Happy to hop on a quick call if that's easier to resolve.

Regards,
Luke Han
Senior Manager, BlueBay Audit

Attachments: bridge_letter_template.docx, log_extract_sample.csv

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Luke Han <luke.han@bluebayaudit.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@fintechco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on report coverage end moment for SOC 2 Type II

Thanks Luke, that wording is exactly what we needed. Samira, we'll prepare the CSV export with event_time in UTC and include the local-to-UTC mapping table for any systems that do not natively store UTC. We'll also draft the bridge letter from the template and upload both artifacts to the drive link you provided by end of day Wednesday.

cc Neha and Priyom for tracking.

Thanks,
Ava
